avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fight against the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and it pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, blue-collar worker teams. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved fund for park purposes toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the 40 trees and 25% required. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council rents land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, from the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

eau-egouts.titre: Drinking water, water supply and sewers
eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and starting work on its water and sewer pipes, both in borough streets and on the main network. It is also awarding several contracts at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, including construction of the oxygen production unit linked to the disinfection project. The replacement of lead service lines, including the portion located on private land, comes up in a large number of decisions.

etapes.titre: Increase in the loan for disinfection
etapes.texte: The City is raising from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the effluent disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks, and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without digging a trench and to redo the pavement, in streets in several boroughs. Each contract includes the replacement of lead water service connections on both the public side and the private side.

The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector and amends the fee schedule of the by-law delegating maintenance of the main network to linked municipalities. A notice of motion is given for a $951,000,000 loan for the renewal of secondary water supply and sewer networks.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary water supply and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord must be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Completion of water pipe rehabilitation work on rue de la Cathédrale postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.
Work site on rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque until December 2027; ozone plant commissioning planned for 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities related to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial support from Québec for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking Québec's ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also assigns two companies the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel by five months, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $574,845.80. The project covers two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, soils, interior divisions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouse commissioning announced for winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: construction in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to redo heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The submission involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural habitats
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 summary of areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, road resurfacing, and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of the work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
DarkSky International's response on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warming centres, and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also extending to other boroughs a Ville-Marie public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness. Finally, it is setting up a framework to accept private donations for shelter and housing.

etapes.texte: The City lends, free of charge, the former Sainte-Bibiane church to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the former Bain St-Denis to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN, for the winter of 2025-2026. The loan of the Bain St-Denis covers 15,406 square feet, from February 1 to April 30, 2026, for about 20 people [CG26 0116].

etapes.titre: Warming centres and outreach workers funded by boroughs
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville extends COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warming centre during the winter of 2025-2026. Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026 [CA26 210012].

The City grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations for new homelessness-related projects and adds $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, over three years, until December 31, 2028, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs. The projects deal with inclusion, cohabitation in public spaces and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Nuit des sans-abri and support on rue Notre-Dame
etapes.texte: The City pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. It also grants $149,520 to the Mission Old Brewery to help people from the encampment area on rue Notre-Dame, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, move toward shelter and housing.

aSurveiller.texte: The Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budgets of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal (OMHM). It transfers or purchases land for social housing, grants subsidies to organizations building housing, and signs funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec. It also amends the by-law requiring developers to include social and affordable housing.

etapes.titre: Two plots of land for social housing
etapes.texte: The City accepts from the Government of Canada half the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre plot of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost. It sells, with no consideration, a 789.6 square metre plot of land on boulevard de l'Acadie to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni, which is to build 26 housing units there, and authorizes a devaluation of $110,000.

The executive committee approves two 2025-2026 funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary shelter and housing search assistance. After a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on the supply of social, affordable and family housing: it now applies only to projects over 18,000 square metres and requires 20% of units to be non-market housing.

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

The City purchases, for $9,293,113 plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square metre plot of land near rue Chatham and rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes 11 lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline set for the sale of the land on rue Chatham and rue William: August 12, 2026.
For the SHDM's 72-unit project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction start by end of 2026, and delivery in May 2028.
Occupancy planned no later than April 30, 2027 for the 350 affordable units at Technopôle Angus.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for lots south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre lot leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 in total, and an 836-square-metre lot leased to a paid-parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

etapes.titre: Loans of land for temporary uses
etapes.texte: The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and a 3,316-square-metre lot to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare itself a free lease of 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for animation activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorized total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Programming and events on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and run the temporary space Esplanade-Louvain, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized, on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, an event-based and temporary use: multimedia activity, shows, street food, a drinking establishment and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and rehabilitated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a $10,311,940.25 contract including taxes to develop a street with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and soil management in the eco-district, for total spending of $15,366,336, and added $2,007,312.15 net to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel will take place in three phases: from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
The loan of the lot for the sunflowers and greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027.
The lease for the animation activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and in 2027.
Four other public places on the site remain to be named by the time the developments are completed, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal starts on October 1, 2026, for three years and a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting collection days and frequency in several boroughs, buying bins and extending food waste treatment contracts while waiting for the Montréal-Est biomethanation centre to start operating. It is also awarding services related to ecocentres and former waste disposal sites. The 2025 report on residual materials management and the accountability report on the 2020-2025 master plan were tabled at the urban agglomeration council.

etapes.titre: Food waste treated outside the city
etapes.texte: The City is extending, first by six months and then by another six months, Recyclage Notre-Dame inc.'s contracts for composting or biomethanation of food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration, until February 28, 2027. The materials are transshipped in Montréal-Est, then composted in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, because the start-up of the Montréal-Est centre is not confirmed.

Several boroughs are awarding hydro-excavation contracts including residual materials treatment, following public call for tenders 25-21256. These services are used for digging with pressurized water near water and sewer pipes, until December 31, 2028.

The City is extending by 12 months Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions's contracts for the collection and disposal of garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers, maintained until October 31, 2027. It is also extending until October 31, 2027 the supply and transport of containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre, a contract assigned to GFL Environmental inc.

etapes.titre: Mattresses, former disposal sites and software
etapes.texte: Recyc-Matelas inc. is awarded the contract for the collection, transport and recovery of mattresses and box springs from the agglomeration's ecocentres, for $734,690.25 taxes included over 28 months. The City is also retaining Consultants AECOM inc. and Terrapex Environnement ltée for studies related to construction on former disposal sites, and is extending Diffusion Solutions Intégrées inc.'s dumping authorization management software.

aSurveiller.texte: Recyclage Notre-Dame inc.'s food waste treatment contracts run until February 28, 2027; the City can end them with 30 days' notice if the Montréal-Est centre becomes fully operational.

Collection schedules change on November 1, 2026 in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where the spacing of garbage collection is being done in two phases, in fall 2026 and fall 2027.
The loan of dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until the contribution runs out, and at the latest by December 31, 2026.
Garbage collection by containers and the supply of containers at the Saint-Laurent ecocentre are ensured until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software is extended from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of the lands, loan by-laws, water main in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It has obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first parcel of land, guaranteed a loan for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for the streets, sewers and water main of the sector. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first parcel of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not entail any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the GALOPH organization that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the public domain of the neighbourhood: soil remediation, sewers and water main, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water main trunk lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which must house a municipal sports and recreation centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first parcel of land must be completed by October 31, 2027 at the latest.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work of parks in several boroughs, from Le Plateau-Mont-Royal to LaSalle, including Le Sud-Ouest and Verdun. It is also taking action on the Grand parc de l'Ouest: repair of stone walls, reconstruction of a culvert, application for a dark sky designation, and listing of an area in the registry of protected natural environments. Several projects first go through soil studies and decontamination before work begins.

etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It also pays money to Verdun for environmental and geotechnical studies at the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and Le Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec for phase 4 of the parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Dog areas, school park and participatory budget
etapes.texte: Anjou redoes the dog park at the parc Lucie-Bruneau and Saint-Laurent sets up a dog park at the parc Alexis-Nihon. Outremont pays $150,000 to the centre de services scolaire to redo the play module at the parc-école Saint-Germain [CA26 16 0052], and Verdun awards a contract for the parc Monseigneur-Langlois, funded by Montréal's participatory budget.

etapes.titre: Public art and land added to a park
etapes.texte: The Service de la culture launches an invitational competition for a work of art at the parc des Eaux-Cachées, in Griffintown. The City also removes a section of the former rue Eadie from the public street domain, to add it to the parc Campbell Ouest; the lot is 810.2 m² [CM26 0704].

Several decisions shift amounts between budgets or add money to ongoing contracts: work supervision for the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, plans for the parc Denise-Morelle. The City also pays $168,472.14 to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension for decontamination and environmental monitoring at the parc George-Vernot [CM26 0887].

aSurveiller.texte: Parc Denise-Morelle: work to be completed in November 2026.
Work of art for the parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation in 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, site compliance in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a follow-up in spring 2027.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of heritage buildings of interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people in situations of residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the area bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal subject to approval.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève indicates it wants to present its project to elected officials starting in mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027, as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks have been announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027, to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding and equipping its police department: a loan for specialized equipment, purchases of vehicles and ammunition, maintenance and service contracts for SPVM buildings. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood stations and premises, lending police officers to the RCMP and the Sûreté du Québec, and accepting grants. Borough councils have adopted motions of support for the SPVM following a shooting that took place on June 22, 2026.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized public safety equipment between 2026 and 2030. The by-law must be approved by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.

The City buys motorcycles, two pickup trucks for the mounted unit (cavalerie), and a patrol boat with its trailer. It also enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police officers' shooting training and requalification.

The City extends janitorial services at headquarters, software maintenance for the computer-aided dispatch system, and the SPVM's mail service. It also awards contracts for meals for detained persons and for carpentry and painting services in the department's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027.
The patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The extension of the computer-aided dispatch software maintenance contract runs until May 4, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system in the mounted unit's (cavalerie) building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
Neighbourhood station 46's "Fèves au lard" (Baked Beans) day takes place on October 23, 2026.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and the loans of the Société de transport de Montréal, sells or leases it land for its equipment, and oversees construction work related to the metro and the REM. It also entrusts the STM with municipal work near the future stations of the blue line and gives it financial support for a sporting event.

etapes.texte: City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the STM's 2026 budget and 2026–2035 capital works program, a balanced budget of $1,804,314,410 (CG26 0022). They also conclude a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, for a maximum of $41,944,604.63 taxes included, plus contingencies.

The City leases to the STM a 2,787-square-metre plot of land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, for parking its agents' vehicles, for a total rent of $49,293. The borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville establishes and removes bus waiting posts on its territory, as part of the bus network overhaul.

The City signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto the metro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It then entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and will pay it up to $3,808,451.29 taxes included.

etapes.titre: Advertising, public access and construction sites
etapes.texte: The City buys advertising space from Astral Affichage in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50 taxes included. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signs an agreement with the STM for access to a vacant lot on boulevard Décarie, Ville-Marie authorizes day and night work in the green line tunnel, and the City does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel over the REM.

The City sells to the STM a 364.3-square-metre plot of land at place Saint-Henri, for $495,150 plus taxes, to expand the entrance building of the Place-Saint-Henri station. It also sells it land in Verdun, for $257,425 plus taxes, for the Rielle ventilation station, and commits to selling it a portion of rue Jean-Brillant, for $115,000 plus taxes, where the STM will build a rectifier station.

etapes.titre: Sporting event and motion on the tunnel boring machine
etapes.texte: The City grants $382,000 to the STM to reinforce bus and metro services during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, and $120,000 to the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau. City council adopts a motion asking the Québec government to study the conditions for keeping the tunnel boring machine "Lisette" in Montréal after the blue line extension.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the land on rue de Louvain begins on October 1, 2026, and lasts three years, at 92 days per year.

The contracts for the work at the Pie-IX and Viau stations must be awarded in August and October 2026; the City's work is integrated in 2028–2029, and the opening of the blue line stations is planned for 2031.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is planned to continue until March 2028.
Authorization from the ministère des Affaires municipales for loans related to the MR-73 and the renovation of surface buildings is expected in November 2026.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bicycles, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed during street construction work. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes an expenditure of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east end
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical works and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 plots of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, with total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to lease about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the repair of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path works under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont files a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships take place in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; stretches along the route are targeted by roadway works in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
The sustainable mobility corridors project resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
